stem: According to the definition provided by the World Health Organization (WHO), what is a defining characteristic of an Adverse Event Following Immunization (AEFI)?

options.text: It must have a proven causal relationship with the vaccine.
It is any untoward medical occurrence that follows immunization.
It only refers to systemic reactions like fever or seizures.
It must occur within the first 24 hours post-vaccination.

explanation: An AEFI is defined broadly as any medical incident occurring after vaccination, regardless of whether the vaccine caused it.
rationale: Consider whether the term 'following' implies a guaranteed cause-and-effect relationship.

optionExplanations.A: The definition specifically states that an AEFI does not necessarily have a causal relationship with the usage of the vaccine.
optionExplanations.B: An AEFI is defined broadly as any medical incident occurring after vaccination, regardless of whether the vaccine caused it.
optionExplanations.C: AEFIs include local reactions, such as injection site swelling, as well as systemic occurrences.
optionExplanations.D: While many reactions occur early, some AEFIs, like those following live vaccines, can occur days or weeks later.

source.hint: Consider whether the term 'following' implies a guaranteed cause-and-effect relationship.
